planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring and plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil once soil has warmed; Frizzle Sizzle is grown chiefly for its dramatically twisted, ruffled cream-and-green variegated foliage rather than for heavy bloom.

directions: Plant rhizomes a few inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun to light afternoon shade. Frizzle Sizzle is a novelty canna selected for its wavy, twisted, almost crumpled cream-and-green variegated leaves, which curl and ruffle along the margins in a way that sets it apart from the broad, flat foliage of most cannas even before the modest orange-red summer flowers appear. Its shorter, more compact stature than large-leaved cannas like Pretoria or Bengal Tiger makes it useful in containers and border plantings where a smaller tropical accent is wanted. Like other cannas it is a heavy feeder that wants consistent moisture and excellent drainage to avoid rhizome rot, and it overwinters in the ground in zone 8 and warmer with a heavy mulch, or can be lifted and stored dry after the first killing frost farther north.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Canna Growing Guide

common_name: Top Pick Brown Crowder Southern Pea (Easy-Harvest Crowder Type)

planting.note: Direct sow seeds 1 inch deep in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun after soil is thoroughly warm; like its sibling Top Pick Pinkeye, this crowder type was bred to set pods concentrated near the top of the plant for faster, cleaner once-over picking during peak Gulf South summer harvest.

directions: Direct sow seeds 1 inch deep in lean to moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once the soil is thoroughly warm. Top Pick Brown Crowder is an improved brown crowder-type Southern pea bred, like the related Top Pick Pinkeye, so pods set concentrated near the top of the plant instead of scattered through the foliage, letting a picker fill a basket quickly during the heaviest part of the summer flush instead of hunting for hidden pods. The tightly packed, squarish brown seeds develop the rich, hearty flavor traditional to crowder-type field peas, and plants hold up well through the hottest, most humid stretch of the season when many other vegetables falter. As with other cowpeas, the roots fix atmospheric nitrogen and improve soil fertility as the crop grows. Harvest pods at the green-shell stage for fresh shelling, or let them dry fully on the plant for long-term storage.
sources: seed catalog reference (Sow True Seed, Rupp Seeds)
